A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiT and EDM generation experiments, convergence measurements and curriculum ablations in Sections 4 and 6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds SiT results and qualitative outputs from longer DiT-L training.

M1.justification: Both versions use progressively accumulated easy-to-hard clusters, SNR-based timestep clustering, EDM quantile clustering and loss-based patience pacing. Section 5 clarifies the same procedure; applying it to SiT does not introduce a new curriculum component. The algorithms are relocated and renumbered.

E1.justification: Both evaluate unconditional FFHQ generation, class-conditional ImageNet and CIFAR-10 generation, and MS-COCO text-to-image generation. The added SiT experiments and longer-trained ImageNet samples retain this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds vanilla SiT and SiT+NaiveCL comparisons against SiT+Ours under velocity and score prediction. Existing DiT/EDM comparisons, curriculum-order comparators, MinSNR and DTR remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds SiT prediction configurations and a separate DiT-L qualitative experiment using 2M iterations and guidance 2.0, beyond the retained 400K-iteration ImageNet setup with default guidance 1.5. Appendix B changes the reported DiT observation sampler from 250-step DDIM to DDPM and specifies EDM quantile intervals instead of v1's uniform-interval description. These reporting revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 1 extends the loss/FID convergence analysis to SiT velocity prediction, testing whether the timestep-difficulty trend persists under another parameterization. Existing hyperparameter, curriculum-order, model-size and noise-schedule analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The Monte Carlo estimators used for the KL analysis are unchanged and merely relocated.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds FFHQ 256×256 SiT FIDs of 7.44/7.69/6.95 for velocity prediction and 9.64/9.77/9.15 for score prediction, ordered Vanilla/NaiveCL/Ours. SiT convergence curves and 2M-iteration DiT-L samples are also new. Existing tabulated numbers and qualitative comparison images are retained; these additions are not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, score-matching objective, KL definitions and Monte Carlo estimators retain their mathematical content. v1's estimator equations reappear in v2 Appendix C. Cluster-boundary notation changes equivalently, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both claim that lower-timestep denoising is harder and that an easy-to-hard curriculum improves generation and convergence while remaining compatible with existing techniques. SiT adds evidence for the retained model-agnostic claim. Correcting 'descending' to 'ascending' difficulty aligns wording with the already-described method.

C2.justification: The curriculum-design discussion removes v1's explicit attribution of anti-curriculum gains to SNR clustering. Appendix I adds a limited qualification concerning hyperparameter choices and model-adaptive curricula, refining the existing future-work discussion. The distributional explanation and broader-impact discussion remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses eight A100 GPUs, optimizer/learning-rate reuse for observation experiments, and that the retained qualitative comparisons use final DiT-B checkpoints. Conversely, v1's dataset-size summaries are omitted. These are documentation changes, not evidence of changed hardware or regenerated comparison images.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to SiT, Karras et al.'s diffusion training-dynamics work and Switch Diffusion Transformer, while removing DiffWave and Weinshall–Amir's curriculum-theory reference. The positioning around denoising difficulty and curriculum learning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify cluster accumulation and pacing and correct the difficulty-order wording. KL estimators, algorithms and metric descriptions move into appendices, an appendix contents page is added, and orthogonality becomes part of Section 6.3. The overall narrative and main-section order remain.

P2.justification: v2 substantially revises typography and page layout, adds the curriculum overview diagram in Figure 3, expands Figure 1 from four to six panels, and reorganizes Table 1 around prediction parameterizations. It also adds five large sample collages in Figures E–I and rearranges retained figures, tables and algorithms.

improvement.justification: The SiT experiments strengthen support for applicability across prediction parameterizations, while Figure 3 and clearer curriculum explanations improve comprehension. Hardware and qualitative-model disclosures modestly improve reproducibility. These gains are limited: the longer-training gallery lacks a matched baseline, and the DDIM-to-DDPM reporting revision is unexplained. The core method and existing quantitative evidence remain intact.
